records.label: spacr.measure.measure_crop.job_callback#1
records.source: The 4-tuple ``(index, average_time, cells, figs)`` that :func:`_measure_crop_core` returns, taken straight off the ``AsyncResult`` -- one result, not the list that :func:`process_measure_crop_results` takes, which is why it is re-wrapped as ``[result]`` below. ``index`` is the position in ``files`` and is translated back through ``index_to_file`` so the ledger entry names the field rather than a number. ``cells`` decides the verdict: the success path leaves the ``np.unique(cell_mask)`` array there, while a plain int ``0`` is the cross-process failure sentinel a worker leaves when it caught its own exception, so only that int records a failure. ``figs`` may be an empty dict -- nothing is drawn unless ``settings['plot']``. Passing the same field twice is safe for the counters (``completed_jobs`` and ``reported_files`` are sets) but would save its figures twice, so the retry loop calls this only for the attempt that actually returned.
records.context: The 4-tuple ``(index, average_time, cells, figs)`` that :func:`_measure_crop_core` returns, taken straight off the ``AsyncResult`` -- one result, not the list that :func:`process_measure_crop_results` takes, which is why it is re-wrapped as ``[result]`` below. ``index`` is the position in ``files`` and is translated back through ``index_to_file`` so the ledger entry names the field rather than a number. ``cells`` decides the verdict: the success path leaves the ``np.unique(cell_mask)`` array there, while a plain int ``0`` is the cross-process failure sentinel a worker leaves when it caught its own exception, so only that int records a failure. ``figs`` may be an empty key-value mapping -- nothing is drawn unless ``settings['plot']``. Passing the same field twice is safe for the counters (``completed_jobs`` and ``reported_files`` are sets) but would save its figures twice, so the retry loop calls this only for the attempt that actually returned.
records.translation: Le 4-uplet ``(index, average_time, cells, figs)`` que renvoie :func:`_measure_crop_core`, pris directement sur l'``AsyncResult`` -- un seul résultat, pas la liste attendue par :func:`process_measure_crop_results`, c'est pourquoi il est réenveloppé en ``[result]`` plus bas. ``index`` est la position dans ``files`` et est retraduit via ``index_to_file`` afin que l'entrée du registre nomme le champ plutôt qu'un nombre. ``cells`` décide du verdict : le chemin de réussite y laisse le tableau ``np.unique(cell_mask)``, tandis qu'un simple int ``0`` est la sentinelle d'échec inter-processus qu'un worker laisse lorsqu'il a intercepté sa propre exception, donc seul cet int enregistre un échec. ``figs`` peut être un dict vide -- rien n'est dessiné sans ``settings['plot']``. Passer deux fois le même champ est sans danger pour les compteurs (``completed_jobs`` et ``reported_files`` sont des ensembles) mais enregistrerait ses figures deux fois, donc la boucle de reprise n'appelle ceci que pour la tentative qui a réellement renvoyé un résultat.
records.review_basis: Independent AI technical review against the English source; no native-speaker signoff.

records.label: spacr.measure.measure_crop.make_error_callback#1
records.source: ``apply_async`` hands the error callback only the exception, so the file has to be closed over. Without this hook a worker that died outright vanished entirely: the exception sat on an AsyncResult nobody read, and the run still printed "Successfully completed run".
records.context: ``apply_async`` hands the error callback only the exception, so the file has to be closed over. Without this hook a worker that died outright vanished entirely: the exception sat on an AsyncResult nobody read, and the processing session still printed "Successfully completed run".
records.translation: ``apply_async`` ne transmet au callback d'erreur que l'exception, donc le fichier doit être capturé par fermeture. Sans ce hook, un worker mort brutalement disparaissait entièrement : l'exception restait sur un AsyncResult que personne ne lisait, et l'exécution affichait quand même "Successfully completed run".

It is used unchanged as the ledger key *and* as the ``reported_files`` entry, so anything else silently loses the match against ``files`` in the ``finally`` sweep and the field is filed a second time as "field produced no result".

It is used unchanged as the ledger structured-data name *and* as the ``reported_files`` entry, so anything else silently loses the match against ``files`` in the ``finally`` sweep and the field is filed a second time as "field produced no result".

records.label: spacr.measure.measure_crop.make_error_callback#3

Call it as ``make_error_callback(file)(exc)`` when raising the exception yourself, which is what the retry loop does on the last attempt -- the ledger counts fields, not tries, so a field that failed twice and then worked must not be reported here at all.

Call it as ``make_error_callback(file)(exc)`` when raising the exception yourself, which is what the retry loop does on the last attempt -- the ledger counts fields, not tries, so a field that failed twice and then worked must not be reported here at all.

Appelez-le sous la forme ``make_error_callback(file)(exc)`` lorsque vous levez vous-même l'exception, ce que fait la boucle de reprise à la dernière tentative -- le registre compte des champs, pas des tentatives, donc un champ qui a échoué deux fois puis réussi ne doit pas du tout être signalé ici.
